segments.caption: Day 4 of 100 Days of Machine Learning: data cleaning, step by step.
8 problems you'll meet in every real dataset, and exactly how to fix each one. Save this one!
Remember our Bangalore flats? 10,000 rows, straight from the websites.
Feed this to a model as it is, and the predictions are garbage. Let's clean it, in order.
Step 1: data profiling. Before fixing anything, look.
Count rows and columns, check each column's type, and count the blanks. Here, price is stored as text, like "1.2 Cr".
Now you know what's broken.
Step 2: fix types and units.
Turn "1.2 Cr" into 120 lakh, and "98 L" into 98. Convert sq m into sq ft. One unit per column, always.
Step 3: standardise categories.
"2 BHK", "2bhk" and "two bedroom" all become the number 2. Koramangala, spelled 4 different ways, becomes one. Otherwise the model thinks they're different places.
Step 4: remove duplicates.
Exact copies are easy. The tricky ones: the same flat posted by 3 brokers, with slightly different prices. Match on area, locality, floor and building, and keep one.
Step 5: missing values. First ask why it's missing.
If the price is missing, that's what we're predicting, so drop the row. If the floor is missing, fill it with the median for that building. And add a column that says it was missing.
Step 6: validity checks. Write simple rules.
Area between 200 and 10,000 sq ft. Built year not in the future. A 12,000 sq ft 1 BHK? Clearly a typo for 1,200, so fix it. If you can't tell, remove it.
Step 7: outliers. Not errors, just extreme.
A 50 crore villa is real, but it will pull a flat price model off course. Keep it, cap it, or model villas separately. We covered this in our outlier treatment video.
Step 8: log everything, and re-check.
Write down every change, and run the profile again. We went from 10,000 rows to 9,300 clean ones. Now the data is ready.
Here's the cleaning checklist, in order.
Profile. Types and units. Categories. Duplicates. Missing values. Validity rules. Outliers. Log and re-check.
Save this, and use it on your next dataset.
Your turn: a flat's price is missing. What's the best approach? Vote in the caption poll!
